newsitem.title: USA: US natgas producers increasingly specialized - NGSA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas producers increasingly specialized - NGSA.

text.p: The largest U.S. natural gas producers during the last decade have increased their role in gas exploration while smaller producers have focused more on managing mature gas fields, the Natural Gas Supply Association said Thursday.

From reviewing 10 years of data from the Energy Information Administration, the NGSA said the top 30 domestic gas producers accounted for 79 percent of new discoveries in 1995, compared with 44 percent in 1986.

The rest of the gas industry increasingly is responsible for additions to the reserve base from revisions, with smaller producers accounting for 36 percent of total gas reserve revisions in 1986, and that segment accounting for 78 percent in 1995.

"Although I have only anecdotal evidence, I believe that the smaller oil and gas companies are getting out of the exploration business because of the need for large capital investments and a high level of technological sophistication that is required to find new gas reserves," said Philip Budzik, NGSA's director of federal regulatory affairs and technical analysis.

Large producers have capital and technology economies of scale best suited to exploration and development of low-cost reserves, while smaller producers have a lower operating cost structure that can be used with enhanced recovery techniques to extend the life of existing gas fields, Budzik said.
